page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scores falling into the bottom 25%, while single-threaded gzip compression is in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, consistently rank in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also perform in the average tier.

Given the balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core performance, this instance is suited for workloads that can leverage parallel processing to overcome weaker single-core speeds. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, database operations, and software compilation, which all registered average tier results in benchmarks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and 1:4 resource density offer a stable baseline for general-purpose enterprise applications, though workloads requiring high single-thread performance or local NVMe storage will face performance and architectural tradeoffs.
